ranking.note: Raised to P1: real hangs in kernel-binding applications (Python/GC finalizers) are a reliability defect at the library boundary, and it is the live alternative that must be decided before the logging work proceeds; moved up from score position 8 for the same reason.
Raised to P1 to match #36768: same deadlock/serialization problem, competing approach; reviewers must decide between the two.
Moved up from score position 17: it is the base of the block-manager/pruning chain (#36854, #36856, #36857) and cannot sit below the PRs it unblocks.
Moved up from score position 18: it is the logging-context foundation under #33847/#30342 (and wallet #30343) and must precede them.
Moved down from score position 5 so it follows its prerequisite #29256; still ahead of the #30342 it unblocks.
Moved down from score position 4: it is the last link of the logging chain (#29256 -> #33847 -> #30342) and depends on both.
Moved down from score position 12: build-target hygiene has no external consumer waiting on it, unlike the API and error-handling work above it.
Moved down from score position 14: optional, compile-time-disabled tooling feature with a single prototype consumer, weakest of the P2 group.

inconsistencies: #36768 and #34775 address the same kernel log-callback deadlock; #36768 is explicitly described as an alternative to #34775. Review #36768 first and decide; only one should land.

#34775's 'allow only one global logging connection' restriction directly contradicts the per-context, multi-connection direction of #33847 and #30342. A design decision is needed before either line proceeds, otherwise one will have to be reworked.

Logging chain order matters: #29256 (context args, based on #34778) -> #33847 (connections attached to contexts, C API shape) -> #30342 (per-context routing). Reviewing #30342 before #33847 wastes effort since the API hooks come from #33847.
Pruning/block-manager chain order matters: #36739 -> #36854 -> #36856 -> #36857. #36856 and #36858 both additionally depend on #36738.

Fatal-error reporting is being restructured by three overlapping PRs: #29700 (util::Result/FlushResult returns), #35646 (removes M_ERROR via util::Expected), #36326 (typed FatalError/FlushError notifications). They should be sequenced deliberately; #35646 is also the stated unblocker for #35570, and #36318 edits the same ValidationState invariants as #35570.
#34132 changes how DB read failures become fatal notifications, which intersects with #29700/#36326's rework of the same notification path, and with #32427's replacement of the block tree DB layer.

#34132, #35662 and #35187 substantively change validation logic as well as the kernel boundary (coins views, PrecomputedTransactionData lifetime, ConnectBlock path); they are kernel+validation PRs and may warrant splitting or joint review with validation reviewers.
result.notes: The category is dominated by one large P2 cluster of chained kernel-API work (logging contexts, block-manager/pruning, fatal-error typing); bands were kept apart mainly where a PR fixes a user-visible reliability defect (P1 logging deadlocks) or is deferrable interface polish/documentation (P3). Draft or paused status (e.g. #32427) was ignored for banding.
